title: ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Bypass: Phishing, Malware Delivery, and Silent Data Exfiltration
content_md: Research by: Alexey Bukhteyev Key Takeaways OpenAI recently introduced Lockdown Mode, an optional advanced security setting designed to protect sensitive user data from prompt injection-based exfiltration attacks. Check Point Research discovered a vulnerability that allowed attackers to bypass Lockdown Mode, rendering its core protections ineffective. The vulnerability exposes a wide attack surface, enabling silent exfiltration of entire chat history, credential theft via phishing, and malware delivery. In ChatGPT Classic, the attack requires zero user interaction: simply having a conversation is enough to trigger silent data exfiltration. Introduction Earlier this year, Check Point Research disclosed a security flaw in ChatGPT’s code-execution runtime that allowed sensitive conversation data to be silently exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server through DNS tunneling, a hidden outbound channel that bypassed the runtime’s network isolation. A fix for this issue was promptly deployed. Moreover, OpenAI later introduced a new security feature: Lockdown Mode .
